newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE says Izetbegovic wins top presidency seat.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says Izetbegovic wins top presidency seat.

text.p: Bosnian's Moslem President Alija Izetbegvic narrowly defeated his hardline Bosnian Serb rival Momcilo Krajisnik to become first head of Bosnia's new collective presidency, election scrutineers announced on Wednesday.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) which organised the election said the completed count gave Izetbegovic 729,034 votes and Krajisnik 690,373.
The third seat on the three-man presidency went to Bosnian Croat candidate Kresimir Zubak who won 342,077 votes. The result was unofficial pending certification.
OSCE mission chief Robert Frowick told reporters: "It appears clear that President Izetbegovic will serve as the president of the presidency."
Izetbegovic, challenged hard by Krajisnik -- a strong supporter of Bosnian Serb independence, will effectively be Bosnia's head of state for the next two years.
The period will be crucial to prospects for the country's reunification under the Bosnian peace agreement last year which ended 43 months of war.
